youtube.title: FREDDIE PONTON
youtube.summary: Freddie Ponton joins Paul Brennan to discuss escalating tensions involving Iran, Russia and Cuba, and how they point to a broader deterioration in global stability. He discusses Iran's refusal to alter its position despite US pressure and questions the credibility of ceasefire arrangements. He also examines Russia's potential response to a deadly drone strike in eastern Ukraine. Freddie also highlights growing US-Cuba tensions, suggesting recent military-to-military contacts may signal significant developments ahead. Discover more from 21st Century Wire or find them on X Follow Freddie on X

youtube.title: TECH TUESDAY
youtube.summary: In this Tech Tuesday, Steven Sykes discusses concerns around digital privacy and emerging technology. He explains how de-googled phones and privacy-focused operating systems are gaining attention as users become more aware of app trackers and data collection. They also touch on age verification systems, stricter ID requirements for phones and SIM cards and how smart TVs track viewer behaviour.

youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Simon Angelo joins Paul Brennan to discuss the Reserve Bank’s OCR decision and Budget 2026. Simon says it lacks a grand vision and criticises the lack of policies to address New Zealand’s declining birth rate and long-term fiscal pressures. They also explore defence spending and the country’s appetite for risk, before turning to investment opportunities driven by AI, quantum computing, and technological innovation. DISCLAIMER: The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They do not constitute personalised financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Listeners should seek guidance from a licensed financial professional who can provide advice based on their individual situation. Discover more from Simon at Wealth Morning

youtube.title: JODIE BRUNING
youtube.summary: Jodie Bruning from Physicians and Scientists for Global Responsibility argues proposed amendments to New Zealand’s HSNO legislation risk weakening environmental and public health protections in favour of agrochemical and biotechnology interests. She claims industry-linked groups have had outsized influence over the policy process, while regulators are increasingly focused on “efficiency” and fast-tracking approvals. For everything you need to Say No to the Gene Technology Bill For more information check out the Daily Telegraph: Democracy lost and a regulatory system in retreat and the PSGR website

youtube.title: KEVIN MORAN
youtube.summary: Kevin Moran joins Paul Brennan to discuss a major victory for Save Our Springs and Golden Bay after NZ Petroleum and Minerals declined Siren Gold a mining licence for Sam’s Creek near the Te Waikoropupū Springs aquifer. Kevin explains concerns about toxic mining waste, arsenic contamination, and the long-term risks to one of the world’s clearest freshwater springs. He says strong public opposition, legal action and environmental concerns helped stop the proposal, though campaigners remain vigilant against future mining attempts. Discover more from Save Our Springs on Facebook

youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart debate grade inflation, changing university pathways and whether tertiary education is delivering value for young people. They discuss rising A-grade rates and increasing student debt, noting that practical skills and trades are being undervalued while more students pursue degrees. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X

youtube.title: SUZY HANSEN
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with long-time UFO researcher Suzy Hansen about decades of sightings, witness accounts, and growing international attention on unexplained aerial phenomena. Suzy discusses the Kaikōura Lights, claims of recurring patterns in New Zealand reports, and her own experiences investigating strange encounters since childhood. Discover more at UFocusNZ

youtube.title: PROF ROB MACCULLOCH
youtube.summary: Talking with Paul Brennan, Professor Robert MacCulloch delivers a scathing critique of the government’s budget, calling the promised return to surplus a “phony” and “reverse-engineered” political exercise designed for election headlines rather than economic reality. He says both National and Labour have failed to address long-term fiscal problems, particularly rising superannuation and healthcare costs – and warns debt could spiral toward crisis levels.

youtube.title: KIRRALIE SMITH
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Kirralie Smith about her New South Wales Supreme Court appeal after being ordered to pay damages over comments relating to transwomen in female sports. Smith discusses the wider impact of the Tickle v Giggle ruling, growing public debate in Australia, and efforts by MPs to strengthen sex-based protections in law. youtube.title: CAMERON BAGRIE
youtube.summary: Cameron Bagrie joins Paul Brennan to break down the Government’s latest Budget, describing it as a “broccoli budget” – tough but necessary. Bagrie says the Government is prioritising fiscal responsibility and infrastructure while shrinking core government spending to move from deficit to surplus.

youtube.title: WEDNESDAY WEBINARS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by Kathryn Ennis-Carter to discuss growing concerns around council-led “managed retreat” policies linked to climate adaptation planning. They examine the use of extreme IPCC modelling, rising insurance levies, flood mapping, iwi involvement in coastal planning, and the influence of central government frameworks on local councils. They also look at Kapiti CALM , a grassroots group challenging Kapiti Coast climate adaptation plans and encouraging residents to engage in council consultations, submissions, and local planning decisions. youtube.title: DOUG CASEY
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Doug Casey about rising Middle East tensions, debt, inflation and global economic instability. Casey says that expanding government debt, currency creation and geopolitical conflict are placing pressure on financial systems and could reshape trade and investment patterns. For further information: Check out Doug Casey's International Man, The Preparation or purchase “The Preparation” Watch Maree's previous interviews with Doug Casey: The Global Culture Trends and How this Affects Finance and Money Management and Global Unrest and the Global Financial Situation is the Calm Before the Storm

youtube.title: FI BUCHET (FiBu)
youtube.summary: Pink Floyd tribute performer Fi Buchet, aka FiBu, joins host Meagan McNamara for NZ Music Month to discuss touring New Zealand with the Pink Floyd Experience. FiBu reflects on the emotional impact of performing The Wall, the strong sense of community surrounding the band, and how its themes of freedom and resistance continue to resonate today. She also shares memories from the anti-mandate protests, talks about her own music collaborations and upcoming instrumental EP, and encourages audiences to catch the final tour performances in Napier* and Palmerston North. *At time of publishing, the Napier show has been cancelled. Discover more from FiBu and the Pink Floyd Experience Get your copy of Heart of the Protest

youtube.title: KANE TITCHENER
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Fluoride Free NZ spokesperson Kane Titchener about a recent US federal appeals court decision that overturned a landmark fluoride ruling that said water fluoridation posed an unreasonable risk to children’s health. Importantly, the decision was based on procedural grounds rather than scientific evidence. Kane says the court did not dispute research linking fluoridation to lower IQ and neurotoxicity and activists are considering an appeal. Discover more from Fluoride Free NZ
